While seeming simple at first glance, remodeling a space can become quickly overwhelming; especially if you want to remodel a kitchen or a bathroom, typically the two most complicated rooms in a home.

I am not going to overwhelm this first post with a ton of information, but over time I will put in resources and advice that just take time to write out and time for you to digest.

In the United States, the National Kitchen and Bath Association is the most recognized governing body of the industry. That being said, as with many other industries, this organization has unfortunately succumbed to shareholders and greed and is more about membership dues and fees than the actual information. Their standards and recommendations are good though, and generally the foundation of a solid layout. Unfortunately, all of their material and resources are very overpriced. Luckily I have similar information that I will post separately by subject, as soon as I have more time.

If you live outside the United States, I am more than happy to look into your country and locality and offer any assistance I may be able to offer.
Where to start on a remodel

That is good for woodworking basics, which I can cover later in another post. That doesn't necessarily translate to a good layout though, I'm here to offer advice, tips and trick for that as well as woodworking stuff

Start and finish the Master. That way when the bathroom remodel goes sideways you always have that space to retire to at the end of the day. And remember count on whatever taking twice as long and being twice as expensive as you initially figure. Especially bathrooms and kitchens.

A good rule of thumb for kitchens that you plan to remodel and live in for at least 5 years is 15 - 20% of the homes value. Bathrooms, especially master baths, can end up being 15% which always surprises people. There's so much tile and plumbing fixtures and specialty light fixtures, not to mention quality labor, it adds up quick. You'll either pay for this in time and labor, or cash. Whichever you have more of. Either way, if you go half-ass, you'll end up doing it twice

We lucked out... well, no, we chose this place, it wasn't really luck at all. But the master bedroom / bath were already re done pretty nicely. Now, only after living here a few years, we're starting to notice where they skimped. But at least they seem to have been following your same methodology.

Additionally; holy fuck, nice kitchen fixtures can be a little pricey! But you do get what you pay for! Replacing the cheap home despot junk with good stuff made a world of difference and was easy!
